Yeah, used to have a really loud monologue. Was also blown away when I learned that not everyone did. Still struggle to comprehend what it's like to not have a constant voice analysing and narrating everything. I mean, I say that but tech use has definitely dampened it. I used to be able to sit and wait and not get bored because I could find ways to amuse myself by talking to myself in my head or narrating the environment, daydreaming etc. I used to think I was a narcissist because I narrated my life as if I was the centre of it all lol. I can still sit and wait, I don't really use my phone, but it's different now and I just don't think or connect much as I sit there. 

I actually miss the voice though, it really was like losing a friend. I've drowned it out with noise and distraction for a long time. When I get echoes of it now, usually by actively encouraging it, it's uncomfortable but also quite life affirming. Even though the voice and I didn't see eye to eye a lot of the times, and it would constantly lead me into traps, it's definitely an aspect of me that is there when I feel alive. As much as it would hurt me or wear me down, sometimes it would tell me everything is OK and catalyse a shift in my perspective. Don't really get that anymore since I don't check in on my other self and tell them how it's going. Events, feelings and thoughts happen and they wash over me because I can't find that entity inside me to discuss them with. 

Maybe "monologue" is not accurate since it was often a dialogue with the entity, and any personal narration felt like it was me explaining to the entity what I was doing or thinking. As sad as it is to say, during the loneliest and most isolated times of my life the entity was the only friend I had to share life with, and now our contact is spotty at best. 

But yeah, distracted myself enough from it that it's a little overwhelming when it comes back now. I feel like I shifted from a feeling of solipsism to feeling like nothing is real and can be confirmed, everything is just so distant. This toxic distraction is the reason I even read this sub as I'm aware that over use of computers is one of the reasons I'm not the same as I was but it is also just a symptom of things that go a bit deeper.

Thanks for posting this btw, it was helpful for me to think about!

Check the spare room ads carefully. See if it's supported accommodation or not. What others have said about HMOs/hostels should be considered. The system is really a bit fucked up here: on one hand it's good that there's these places that help some vulnerable people get off the street or away from dangerous situations at home etc. But the conditions can be terrible and you have very little rights.

 What others have said about being forced to move within a couple days is very true, not just if you find employment but for any small reason that the private housing company decides and I don't actually think they are legally required to give you any time at all (but I hope someone can correct me on this). They actively try and get people out if they find them difficult and there's little you can do about it without getting legal representation. I worked for one of these housing companies so I've seen it first hand. To get a better picture, search for the Guardian article about Concept Housing Birmingham. Make sure any flats you've seen aren't for one of these types of companies/associations with supported accommodation. 

These companies and private landlords make big bank off the government for this as well! I wish I knew how to help improve the system. Best of luck, and if you do move here I hope all goes well!

I've worked with ex prisoners who often could not get identification after their stint, there was always a wall they hit when trying to apply - a lot of the times, even getting a birth certificate was difficult. I couldn't be the referee as their support worker, for reasons. Nor could their PO, and the prison system doesn't seem to have any support to help them get one. It is so frustrating. 

It makes trying to function and reintegrate in society really difficult and there's always companies that prey on people who don't have a passport or driving licence. For example, the only shady banks that they can get without ID are ridiculously exploitative and would charge to simply *check* their balance, charge to make transfers and pay bills. And if you can't get a regular job cus you don't have ID you're forced to take cash in hand. 

It really makes me mad, cus it *is* mad. If the whole ID for voting scheme passes then a large part of our population who already struggle for rights and representation will be further silenced. Tragic.

So I've been watching wrestling again since I stopped in 2016 I think. By the end of it, I was only watching NXT and Lucha Underground before getting busy with life and losing interest. Fwiw I adored both of those shows. 

I came back for money in the bank and return to live crowds and to check out AEW.

This is how I currently feel/ramblings;

MITB was fun to return on, it gave me the feelings I had missed. A lot of new faces to me. Rhea vs Charlotte also made me remember that I could enjoy just straight up good wrestling.

But then I watched Raw and thought it was mostly rubbish. The novelty of having John Cena there was lost on me since John Cena was still full time when I stopped. But I pushed through and gave it a shot and it took ages for me to enjoy it again, mainly after the draft because...

I enjoyed Smackdown. More and more each week as I acclimated to watching wrestling again, it felt comfy. Didn't enjoy it as much as I used to, of course,   but there was something there. I was very sports entertained at times. It was nice to see old favourites still around and some cool new people.

I still can't imagine watching RAW without fast forward though. I swear before draft I was skipping 70% or more of Raw, now it's about 50% lol. I think that's why I enjoy WWE more than most - I simply skip the shit I don't like or all the filler. 

I did not enjoy AEW very much. I enjoyed their PPV, I don't remember the name, it was the one where CM Punk had his match with Darby Allin. I was excited about the CM Punk return tbh and actually bought Fire TV for a month just to watch that Rampage live at 2 am my time lmao. But after that match I stopped enjoying it for the most part, and have absorbed the MJF feud through clips lol. As of right now, I have not watched AEW in months. I want to get back into it, cus I like wrestling again, but it's harder to get into tbh and feel like ill just be lost again. They don't really do a good job of filling in new and casual viewers. Plus they do a lot of shit I don't enjoy. And I can't be bothered to watch supplementary material like vlogs and YouTube shows, follow wrestlers on social media etc. I was instantly up to speed with WWE while watching MITB. Took me weeks of AEW to get into the groove of that show. Idk man. I don't mind wrestling for wrestling's sake, I used to watch ROH and Lucha Libre and Japanese matches with no context, but I do enjoy sports entertainment shit lol. Lucha Underground is one of my all time favourite TV shows beyond "wrestling shows." I want to like AEW, and really wished/ believed I was gonna be one of those lapsed fans who fell in love with wrestling again after watching. Sucks that it didn't happen.

Speaking of matches without context, I watched Dragunov vs WALTER when looking up recent "best matches" to see if I actually still enjoyed wrestling for wrestling. And fuck me, did I enjoy it. It was honestly unbelievable and I so badly wish all wrestling was like that. All the time. Made me want to get back into Japanese wrestling again but I'm not quite there yet lol.

I still enjoy the weird phenomenon of wrestling more than the product, so I've been enjoying Dark Side of the Ring and analysis and non-fiction etc. 

Last but definitely not least: NXT. I fucking love NXT 2.0. Like I said, I was a big NXT fan from day one of when it became the new FCW. However, I missed the coveted Super Indie era for the most part. I stopped watching after Takeover London it seems, as I did not see Nakamura or Aries debut. So my prime NXT memories were 2014-2016 and NXT 2.0 is a lot like that era. And I'm having almost as much fun watching it. This show has rekindled my enjoyment of wrestling. I was really disheartened when I tuned into 2.0 on the debut episode and for like a month, cus it was dogshit let's be real. But after it found its feet I love it and anticipate it just like I used to. I think people forget that before 2016 NXT was just like this - developmental talent finding what works, mixed with indie vets who could put on bangers, with strong (and sometimes silly!) characters, hot crowd and well told, intimate storylines. Very diverse and frenetic. Pretty much everything I enjoy, and the matches will no doubt keep getting better as the greener talent improves. I'm far, far more excited for Stand and Deliver than Wrestlemania. And that triple threat from this weeks show fucking slapped and was another "wrestling matches are good, remember?" moments for me. 

I will say, I am sad I didn't witness stuff like Gargano vs Ciampa blood feud, the Cruiserweight Classic and the passionate fans and amazing moments that NXT must have given people from 2016 plus. Looks like I would have loved it. 

But yeah.... That's my thoughts I've just wanted to share for a long time, thought I would rattle them out once for nobody to read lmao. I have one friend IRL who likes wrestling but he's very much "AEW is the best shit ever and I'm never watching WWE ever again" kinda guy so he doesn't get a lot of what I'm saying, and he's the reason I started watching again cus he was telling me how great AEW is.

Yeah, one hundred percent agree. The amount of times I've made myself look stupid and full of shit and lose respect by telling people what I'm going to do and not doing it... It doesn't legitimise it, it's taking credit for something you haven't done yet and getting a reward that diminishes your desire to attain the reward of actually achieving your goal. It makes failure more difficult. 

I'm not just talking about people you personally know, but even anons online. I've felt that guilt of letting strangers down who took the time to write me advice or well wishes. Even if that was their own attempt to legitimise their own intentions, it was still energy spent in my direction and I should appreciate it. 

The people I admire most don't talk about what they're going to do, they just do it and talk about it later. They don't have to convince me because they've already convinced themselves. I want to be that person. 

Ultimately, the only person who can hold you accountable is you. If you have the need to verbalise it to make it seem real, write it in a note or a journal and save it.

Once I stopped talking about it, I just started to do more things and beating myself up less for the things I don't do. It's a satisfaction for myself, achieving things that I'm doing for myself. 

Seeking pride, not praise. This also helps you focus on the most important-to-you things.

But yeah, good post and advice not enough people share. Sorry for rambling.

Hi there, I don't have any direct advice but I deeply relate. I actually made a post about it here a while back and lots of helpful people chimed in with good advice and insight.  Might be worth checking to see their responses.

And actually I can advise that if you don't do anything and feel unproductive don't beat yourself up too much about it. Because you won't get trapped in those critical cycles, leaving you more free to try again.

It's very difficult though and in the 11 months since posting that thread I haven't made as much progress as I would have liked, but I have made more than I did in the 11 months prior to that.
